look_here_first: FIRST FIND WHERE THE DENSE FLOWER HEADS GROW. E. ophthalmica generally forms a small, prostrate, hairy mat (stems typically 6–22 cm) ending in round, crowded HEADS of tiny cyathia, at the tips of main stems and short LEAFY side branches. E. hirta produces both terminal AND axillary flower heads, often axillary on longer leafless stalks, and is often taller. E. ophthalmica has opposite asymmetric leaves 4–13 mm long with coarse tiny teeth, hairy capsules, and distinct narrow/subulate sometimes divided stipules at the nodes. A reddish leaf mark can occur but is NOT diagnostic; do not rely on flower-head shape without location and fruit/stem verification.

synonyms: Euphorbia hirta var. ophthalmica (Pers.) Allem & Irgang
taxonomic_note: Accepted Euphorbia ophthalmica Pers. (POWO/WCVP; Flora of North America). Formerly combined with or treated as variety of E. hirta; diagnostic terminal-only small heads, prostrate habit and small leaves separate these concepts.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbiaceae; Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum. Opposite leaves, milky latex, cyathia (tiny reproductive structures), 3-lobed dry fruit.
morphology_keys.habit: Usually prostrate, rarely ascending, annual (occasionally short-lived perennial) from taproot; slender shoots 6–22 cm. A low spreading habit is suggestive, never sufficient alone.
morphology_keys.stems: Fine short appressed hairs (strigillose) mixed with longer spreading hairs (hirsute), often both on the same plant.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; ovate to oblong, 4–13 × 3–7 mm, asymmetric base, coarse fine teeth (coarsely serrulate), usually with 3 veins emerging near base; center may carry red blotch but many leaves do not.
morphology_keys.stipules: Distinct, narrow subulate-filiform scales, entire or divided into 2–4 slender triangular/threadlike segments, 0.9–1.5 mm, hairy; lacking dark round glands at base. A magnified true node is needed to distinguish from ordinary hairs.
morphology_keys.flowering_cluster: Dense CAPITATE terminal glomerules; at ends of main stems or very short leafy side shoots. Small reduced bractlike leaves occur beneath them. Unlike E. hirta, not separate axillary flower heads on long leafless stalks.
morphology_keys.cyathia: Tiny involucres about 0.5–0.7 × 0.4–0.6 mm with fine hairs; four yellow-green to pinkish glands, with thin white/pink rims or very small appendages, sometimes without obvious appendages.
morphology_keys.fruit: Ovoid three-lobed capsule 1–1.2 × 1–1.3 mm, strigillose (finely appressed-hairy), not smooth/glabrous.
morphology_keys.seed: Orange-brown to pinkish, narrowly ovoid, sharply four-angled; 0.7–0.9(–1.1) × about 0.5 mm; usually shallow wrinkling and 3–6 faint transverse ridges, occasionally smooth-looking.

comparisons.key_distinctions: E. ophthalmica and E. hirta both have hairy leaves and tight heads: inspect cluster POSITION. Ophthalmica has strictly terminal heads (on main or short leafy lateral branches), shorter generally prostrate stems and 4–13 mm leaves. Hirta bears terminal PLUS axillary heads (often at ends of elongate leafless peduncles). E. hypericifolia also has dense heads but stems/capsules are glabrous and it has triangular fused stipule scales. E. nutans has leafier, less condensed cyathial clusters and GLABROUS fruit. E. maculata is a mat with cyathia solitary/small clusters rather than large capitate glomerules, and hairs spread over capsule faces.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Ophthalmica: follow stems to the END of the flower-head cluster
steps: Photograph WHOLE prostrate plant with soil contact, including tips of multiple stems.
Trace each compact cyathium head backward: is it at a stem tip or a short LEAFY side shoot, instead of an elongated leafless axillary flower stalk?
At 10–20× find two sizes of stem hair, then inspect a real three-lobed capsule for fine appressed hairs.
Inspect opposite 4–13 mm leaves for asymmetric bases and little teeth (ignore whether they have a red spot).
At 20–30× distinguish subulate stipules from leaf or stem hairs at the node.
For a final difficult determination, dissect a mature capsule and photograph actual seeds with millimeter scale.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Do not teach terminal flower heads alone as a unique trait: many Euphorbia make them. The critical comparison with E. hirta is TERMINAL ONLY vs TERMINAL PLUS AXILLARY glomerules, supported by habit, leaf dimensions, hair pattern, capsule and seed. The initial face photograph does not resolve tiny stipules, a hairy capsule or seed ridges.
